rationale: Both catch the residual async_chunk default-value inconsistency (matching the ground-truth Low comment), and neither surfaces the amy-why design question, so recall is comparable. X's precision is undermined by two fabricated/contradicted claims: it asserts the PR's E2E evidence was 'stream=False only' when the ground-truth review explicitly describes a stream=True vs stream=False comparison, and it cites a 'red' buildkite CI gate with no supporting evidence in the provided data. Y's findings are all accurately grounded, including a well-reasoned note that the splitting logic drops hidden-shape alignment in favor of scheduled-token alignment — directly touching the latent multi-axis gap later fixed by PR #4910, which X never raises. X is more concretely actionable (specific tests to add, file:line evidence), but Y's higher trustworthiness and gap detection outweigh that.
